NVDA.rationale: NVDA presents a strongly attractive fundamental profile across all three pillars. Pillar 1 (fundamentals): Q1 FY2027 revenue of $81.6B (+85% YoY), net income of $58.3B at 71.5% net margin, operating cash flow of $50.3B, and a fortress balance sheet (D/E = 0.043, $195.5B equity vs $8.5B debt) represent best-in-class large-cap fundamentals. The franchise is structurally dominant with ~86% data center GPU market share, CUDA software lock-in, and broadening demand (Hyperscale $37.9B +115%, AI Clouds/Enterprise $37.4B +74%). Q2 guide of $91B (+95% YoY) confirms acceleration, not deceleration. Pillar 2 (valuation): Trailing PE of 31.3x sits at the absolute floor of its 365-day range (30.6–66.8x), representing ~40% compression from the one-year median in the low-to-mid 50s. P/B at 25.6x is also at its 365-day floor. The stock at $204.87 is only ~12% above its quarterly-ago level while EPS nearly tripled YoY — the market has not re-rated to reflect the new earnings power. Pillar 3 (near-term catalyst): The $110B shareholder return plan announced 2026-06-11 (2,400% dividend increase, $80B buyback) is a dated capital-allocation catalyst signaling management conviction in durable FCF. Oracle's $70B FY2027 capex plan, the SpaceX-Google $30B GPU lease deal, and Alphabet's $80B AI infrastructure raise provide fresh demand validation. Vera CPU ($200B TAM, $20B expected H2 FY2027) opens a new revenue stream. Key risk: margins at historic peaks (74.9% gross, 81.7% ROE) are as good as it gets; any hyperscaler capex deceleration would compress both earnings and multiples. China market share at zero adds regulatory noise. The earnings yield of 3.2% trails the 10-year Treasury at 4.45%, a structural headwind. However, the combination of dominant franchise, accelerating growth, historic valuation discount, and a credible near-term capital-return catalyst supports a score above +0.5.

Nvidia holds roughly 86% of the AI GPU market. Its closest direct competitors, AMD and Intel, have single-digit shares.

Nvidia expects $20 billion in Vera CPU sales in the back-half of fiscal 2027... Vera Rubin includes 7 chips across 5 racks, compared to Blackwell's main compute rack.
The U.S. Department of Commerce closed a loophole that had allowed advanced AI chips from Nvidia and AMD to be exported to Chinese firms operating outside of China.
